scope: Core-level block-vs-sequential cost of a padded 256 dispatch

provenance.superseded_note: v1 used the standalone harness because oflm was believed unscriptable; it is scriptable (stdin EOF is /bye), and the closure sweep therefore runs the shipped binary
provenance.closure_driver: build/src/oflm, HEAD dcd6e7d1 + the Phase 27 engine.cpp changes
provenance.timing: runner PREFILL_TIME, one process per side, /clear between prompts (resets the profilers)

shipped_crossover_before_provenance: engine.cpp, inherited from the Qwen3.6-35B MoE layer-major case
v1_why_wrong: v1 reported 'the smallest SAMPLED length at which the padded block is no slower'. Its own table is 64 -> 1.18 and 128 -> 0.72, which crosses near 81; the rule returned the first grid point past the crossing, i.e. 128, not the crossing itself. A constant chosen from a six-point grid overcharges every prompt between the crossing and the next sampled point.
v2_rule: linear fit through the sequential side against the median flat block cost; the crossing is where the two cost curves meet, not the nearest sampled point

applied.engine.cpp: two constants chosen by capability, not by model name
applied.layer_major_override: OFLM_OPEN_LAYER_MAJOR: unset = automatic preference, 0 = force off, nonzero = force on wherever layer_major_ok() is true (Phase 32)
applied.why_96_not_78: the crossing is fitted at 78 and the first clear win at 92 (0.85); 96 keeps a small margin over the single unpinned pass behind each point, and rounds onto the 8-token grid the sweep used
applied.impact_on_the_27_6_matrix: none: every length in that matrix is >= 255 engine tokens, far above either constant
applied.impact: prompts of 80..127 engine tokens used to take a padded 256-wide block at 33.5 s when stepping them costs 24-55 s; that range now steps, and 96..127 pads

evidence.artefact: not committed: runs/ is scratch (.gitignore). Reproduce with: python crossover_local.py --block-min 1

linear_fit.cross_check: 425.49 ms/token is 2.35 tokens/s, which matches the runner's own 'Average prefill speed: 2.34711 tokens/s' printed by /status -- the two independent instruments agree

evidence.block_cost_flat_note: 33.1-34.5 s across 56..136 engine tokens: the cost is the dispatch width, not the real row count

superseded_sweep.artefact: not committed: runs/ is scratch. Reproduce with the superseded tail_crossover.py, kept as the record of how 128 was produced
superseded_sweep.why_superseded: the block side ran under the shipped policy, so every length below the crossover fell through to sequential -- two sequential runs per point, whose ratio is noise around 1.0. Counting those non-decisive points produced a spurious 'measured crossover' of 104. The fine sweep forces the block side with OFLM_OPEN_GEMM_BLOCK_MIN=1 so every point really is a padded pass.
superseded_sweep.kept_because: it is the only sweep that measures the SHIPPED policy end to end, and its >= 128 points agree with the fine sweep

route_matrix_after_the_change.artefact: not committed: runs/ is scratch. Reproduce with: python route_matrix.py --mode block
route_matrix_after_the_change.note: that run started BEFORE engine.cpp was changed, so it imported the old 128 into expected() and marked 96, 127 and 383 FAIL although the engine did exactly what 96 requires; the re-run with the constant at 96 is runs/route-matrix-block-<later>

corroboration.source: oflm serve, shipped binary, one resident server
corroboration.note: flat across the 256 boundary, the padding signature, measured through the runtime
